messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure arises in the method ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>) which calls getShortClassName(String) with the name of the class. The getShortClassName(String) method attempts to extract the short name from the fully qualified class name by finding the last dot and inner class separator '$'. However, it does not handle the array class name format correctly.

Array class names in Java have a binary representation that typically includes characters such as '[' at the start and type descriptors ending with a semicolon for object arrays. The bug report confirms that when passing an array, the returned short class name incorrectly has a semicolon appended to the end (e.g., "String;"). 

Looking at the code of getShortClassName(String), there is a comment placeholder about handling array encoding, but the logic to strip the array type encoding is missing. The method simply looks for the last '.' and '$' characters and extracts the substring after the last '.' which in the case of arrays will be something like "[Ljava.lang.String;" and thus it returns "String;" which includes the trailing semicolon because it does not strip the array type encoding.

The test expects the short class name for String[].class to be "String[]" but instead it receives "String;" which is due to the missing logic for stripping array notation and converting array types to their human-readable form.

No recent issues relate to this problem, so it is solely a bug in the getShortClassName(String) method, specifically its lack of handling for array class names and missing logic where indicated by the comment: "// Handle array encoding".

This explains the incorrect trailing semicolon and the failure of the test case test_getShortClassName_Class.

The fix would be to implement the stripping of array encoding (like removing leading '[' and replacing type descriptors with simple names and adding '[]' as appropriate) inside getShortClassName(String).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
